summary: Grading is a pure function of the four submitted plan files and static, hash-pinned verifier data: no randomness, clock, network, readiness wait or order-dependent comparison affects the reward, and plan-internal ordering is accepted in any order with exact integer cost arithmetic.

files_read: environment/app/days/day-1.json (lines 1-30 read; whole file regex-swept for non-integer numerics and key fields)
environment/app/days/day-2.json (whole file regex-swept for non-integer numerics and key fields)
environment/app/days/day-3.json (whole file regex-swept for non-integer numerics and key fields)
environment/app/days/day-4.json (whole file regex-swept for non-integer numerics and key fields)

tests/days/day-1.json.gz..day-4.json.gz (binary gzip; content bound by roster SHA-256 which equals the manifest hash of the corresponding environment/app/days/<day>.json, asserted at tests/test_outputs.py:36)

checks_performed: Traced tests/test.sh: fixed reward initialisation, pytest run with -p no:randomly and -p no:cacheprovider, reward from exit code only; mktemp RUN_DIR is scratch cwd and never compared (D-3 pattern).

Traced tests/test_outputs.py: reads verifier-owned targets.json, roster.json and gzip day copies; SHA-256 and count assertions make the day data fixed; PLANS defaults to /app/plans (STAND_PLANS unset by test.sh).

Compared roster.json sha256 values (19c101fd..., d2bbbc54..., 7f6e617f..., 7ed60ada...) with packet-manifest hashes of environment/app/days/day-1..4.json: all four match, so the verifier data is identical to the candidate-visible data and cannot drift between runs.

Confirmed tests/targets.json and environment/app/days/targets.json have the same manifest hash and identical contents; tests/check_plan.py and environment/app/tools/check_plan.py have the same manifest hash.

Traced check_plan.evaluate: per-stand occupancy is sorted by (arrive, depart, tid) before buffer checks; wingtip check is pairwise over all members; cost is an order-independent sum. Plan list order and stand key order are therefore accepted in any order, matching stand-rules.md:65-66 ('in any order').

Regex-swept all four day files for decimal/exponent numerics: none, so walk_metres, passengers, pax and bus cost are integers and the cost comparison at tests/test_outputs.py:55 is exact integer arithmetic with no float summation-order sensitivity.
Checked for wall-clock, random, network, subprocess, threading or sleep use in test_outputs.py, check_plan.py and test.sh: none.

Checked dependency pinning: both Dockerfiles pin the python:3.13-slim-bookworm image by digest; verifier pins pytest==9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2; verifier runs with network no-network; grading imports only stdlib json/gzip/hashlib/os/sys plus pytest.
Checked timing: evaluation is polynomial over at most 63 stands / 360 turns / 1413 transfers per day against a 1800 s verifier timeout; no readiness waits exist.
Checked solution/solve.sh: copies static committed plans and checks them with the shipped checker; no stochastic step in the reference path.
Checked task.toml artifacts ['/app/plans/'] with environment_mode separate: only the plan files cross into the verifier, so agent-side mutable state under /app cannot vary grading.

coverage_sweep.category: Fixed fixtures / stable seeds; boundary cases guaranteed
coverage_sweep.reason: No generated corpus: the four graded days are committed files bound by SHA-256 and count assertions; targets are committed constants.

coverage_sweep.category: Evaluation clock fixed when expiry/time windows are graded
coverage_sweep.reason: Time windows are integer minutes from the day file; no wall-clock call anywhere in grading.

coverage_sweep.category: Dependencies pinned and required inputs local
coverage_sweep.reason: Base images pinned by digest, pytest and ctrf plugin pinned, verifier has no network, grading reads only /tests data and the submitted plans. Transitive pytest dependencies are not pinned but are installed at image build and cannot plausibly change a stdlib-only integer comparison; recorded as non-finding.

coverage_sweep.category: Ordering: sorted where required, equivalent orderings accepted otherwise
coverage_sweep.reason: Contract allows any order; checker sorts occupancy before buffer checks and computes an order-independent integer sum; duplicate/missing detection is set-based.
No services, sleeps or waits; pure file evaluation well within timeout.
All day numerics are integers (regex sweep), so cost is an exact Python int compared with an int target.
mktemp RUN_DIR only sets pytest cwd; all paths in test_outputs.py are absolute or relative to the test file, so the random name cannot affect grading.

coverage_sweep.category: Repeated clean-run stability of correct and incorrect submissions
coverage_sweep.reason: Static trace (not executed): with fixed plans, fixed day data and fixed targets, evaluate() is deterministic, so the reference (cost == target) passes and the shipped-planner plans (costs above target per task.toml) fail on every run.

rules: buffer rule between consecutive turns on a stand
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Same stand assignment serialized with turns in reverse order: evaluate() sorts occ by (arrive, depart, tid) before the buffer comparison, so validity and cost are identical.

rules: stand may be omitted or empty (stand-rules.md:66-67)
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Wingtip stand omitted from plan: plan['stands'].get(a, []) yields empty list deterministically; no KeyError or order dependence.

rules: verifier uses its own copy of the day
candidate-visible day file defines the problem
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Roster SHA-256 equals manifest hash of each environment day file, so the graded instance is the same bytes the candidate optimised against on every run.
Plan exactly on target (reference): integer equality with <= passes stably; no float rounding can push it over.
